cards.name: Contour1
cards.summary: CorelDRAW Contour tool preset. Shipped preview (the .pst file's own embedded thumbnail, not a script render) shows an inside contour on a square: about six evenly spaced concentric steps closing in on a small core, each step a vertical light-to-dark fountain, running from pale sky blue at the outer edge to deep blue with a violet-indigo core, like a stepped tunnel. Applied to your own object it carries the step count, offset, direction and colour settings, not the blue square.
use_for: stepped 'tunnel' or depth panel behind a headline
op-art or topographic concentric frames
retro inset badges and buttons
avoid: A single offset outline (sticker cut line, bleed, keyline): use one Outside step or Object > Path > Offset; this preset makes many steps.
Thin or detailed shapes such as small text: inside steps collapse and self-overlap; use fewer steps or a bigger, simpler shape.
A smooth fade: a contour is visibly stepped; use a fountain fill instead.
Scripting this exact preset: its parameter block is undocumented; rebuild the look with Shape.CreateContour.
A light centre with a dark rim: use Contour2, which runs the colours the other way.
cards.applies_to: one vector object (closed shape, curve or artistic text) selected with the Contour tool: it builds a live Contour group of concentric steps from that object's outline; editing the source object updates the steps
cards.how_to_apply: Toolbox > Effect Tools > Contour (Automation.InvokeItem("441d6b88-877e-4d00-951f-4521b9987650")): select the object, then pick 'Contour1' in the Preset list on the property bar. Script: the harvest records no call that applies a .pst preset (its 62-byte parameter block is undocumented); the file is Draw/Presets/Contour/Contour1.pst in the CorelDRAW install folder. Scripted substitute: Shape.CreateContour(Direction=cdrContourInside, Offset, Steps=about 6, BlendType, OutlineColor, FillColor, FillColor2, SpacingAccel, ColorAccel, EndCapType, CornerType, MiterLimit) set to match the preview (approximate; not tested by the harvest).

verified.note: Shipped preview: about six evenly spaced inside-contour steps on a square, pale sky blue rim to a small violet-indigo core, each step lighter at top, as described.

review.changes: install path in how_to_apply made relative (no machine paths)

cards.name: Contour2
cards.summary: CorelDRAW Contour tool preset. Shipped preview (the .pst file's own embedded thumbnail, not a script render) shows an inside contour on a square whose outer step is a vertical fountain from bright cyan (top) to indigo (bottom); about five tightly spaced steps lighten inward and stop well short of the centre, leaving a large pale sky-blue core: dark rim, light glowing centre, the reverse colour direction of Contour1. Applied to your own object it carries the step, offset and colour settings, not the blue square.
use_for: bevelled or embossed-looking button and panel frames
inner-glow frame around a photo or headline area
stepped neon-like borders on badges and stickers
avoid: A single offset outline (sticker cut line, bleed, keyline): use one Outside step or Object > Path > Offset; this preset makes many steps.
Thin or detailed shapes such as small text: inside steps collapse and self-overlap; use fewer steps or a bigger, simpler shape.
A smooth fade: a contour is visibly stepped; use a fountain fill instead.
Scripting this exact preset: its parameter block is undocumented; rebuild the look with Shape.CreateContour.
Many steps reaching the centre: use Contour1, which steps all the way in to a small core.
cards.applies_to: one vector object (closed shape, curve or artistic text) selected with the Contour tool: it builds a live Contour group of concentric steps from that object's outline; editing the source object updates the steps
cards.how_to_apply: Toolbox > Effect Tools > Contour (Automation.InvokeItem("441d6b88-877e-4d00-951f-4521b9987650")): select the object, then pick 'Contour2' in the Preset list on the property bar. Script: the harvest records no call that applies a .pst preset (its 62-byte parameter block is undocumented); the file is Draw/Presets/Contour/Contour2.pst in the CorelDRAW install folder. Scripted substitute: Shape.CreateContour(Direction=cdrContourInside, Offset, Steps=about 5, BlendType, OutlineColor, FillColor, FillColor2, SpacingAccel, ColorAccel, EndCapType, CornerType, MiterLimit) set to match the preview (approximate; not tested by the harvest).

verified.note: Shipped preview: outer step cyan at top to indigo at bottom, about five tight steps lightening inward to a large pale sky-blue core, as described.

review.changes: install path in how_to_apply made relative (no machine paths)

cards.name: Dimension1
cards.summary: CorelDRAW dimension-line preset (style 'Dimension1' in DimensionPresets.cdss; not rendered, read from the file's own values): a hairline black dimension line (outline.width 762 = 0.076 mm, about 0.22 pt, CorelDRAW's hairline) with no arrowheads (outline.leftArrow / rightArrow empty); a black Arial 12 pt label (2 decimal places, unit shown, leading zero, label centred, placement code 0, read as above the line if the file's textPlacement follows cdrDimensionPlacement (0 above, 1 within, 2 below; mapping not checked)), no box; extension lines on, dynamic text on, radial-label setting radialInsideOutside 0 (not decoded).
use_for: minimal, arrow-free measurement lines on packaging dielines and product spec sheets
exact sizes such as 12.70 mm or 3.25 in on dielines, laser / CNC cut sheets and print specs
client presentation boards that show live sizes next to the artwork
avoid: Expecting a rendered look: no thumbnail exists, the description comes from the preset's stored values (line width, arrowhead path, text settings); check it on the page before a job depends on it.
Hairline output: a 0.076 mm line can vanish on large-format or low-resolution output; thicken the outline after applying.
Files going to Illustrator or Photoshop: the dimension object is CorelDRAW-only and arrives as plain lines and text that stop updating; convert to curves first if the look must survive.
Large plans where values like 1234.56 clutter the drawing: use a 0-decimal preset (Dimension7-11).
Engineering drawings that need arrowheads: use Dimension4-11.
cards.applies_to: dimension objects drawn with CorelDRAW's Dimension tools (Parallel, Horizontal or Vertical, Angular, Segment; Toolbox > Dimension flyout): sets the dimension line's outline and arrowheads, the label's font and colour and the label format (decimal places, units shown, placement, box); not for ordinary lines, text or callouts
cards.how_to_apply: Pick a dimension tool (Parallel Dimension: Toolbox > Dimension flyout, Automation.InvokeItem("f1b16e8a-9f6f-05b4-4610-451172f5fff2")) and choose 'Dimension1' where the tool lists its presets (the harvest records the preset file, not the property-bar control): Custom Data/DimensionPresets.cdss in the CorelDRAW install folder, style Dimension1. Script: no harvested call applies a .cdss dimension preset; reproduce it with Layer.CreateLinearDimension(..., Precision=2, ShowUnits=True, Placement=0, BoxedText=False, LeadingZero=True, OutlineWidth=hairline, Arrows=none, TextFont="Arial", TextSize=12, ...) or edit an existing dimension through Shape.Dimension (Precision, Placement, BoxedText, ShowUnits, Outline) (untested).

verified.note: No thumbnail (dimension preset, not visual); every stated value checked against DimensionPresets.cdss and matches.

review.changes: install path in how_to_apply made relative (no machine paths)

cards.summary: CorelDRAW dimension-line preset (style 'Dimension8' in DimensionPresets.cdss; not rendered, read from the file's own values): a hairline black dimension line (outline.width 762 = 0.076 mm, about 0.22 pt, CorelDRAW's hairline) with closed slim triangular arrowheads at both ends (about 1.9:1 long); a black Arial 12 pt label (0 decimal places, unit shown, leading zero, label centred, placement code 2, read as below the line if the code follows cdrDimensionPlacement (0 above, 1 within, 2 below; mapping not checked)), boxed (boxAroundText 1); extension lines on, dynamic text on, radial-label setting radialInsideOutside 1 (not decoded).
use_for: technical and fabrication drawings where arrowed dimension lines are expected
signage, exhibition and room plans where whole numbers read faster
labels that must stand out on busy drawings (boxed value)
client presentation boards that show live sizes next to the artwork
avoid: Expecting a rendered look: no thumbnail exists, the description comes from the preset's stored values (line width, arrowhead path, text settings); check it on the page before a job depends on it.
Hairline output: a 0.076 mm line can vanish on large-format or low-resolution output; thicken the outline after applying.
Files going to Illustrator or Photoshop: the dimension object is CorelDRAW-only and arrives as plain lines and text that stop updating; convert to curves first if the look must survive.
Small parts or tolerances: 0 decimals rounds 12.7 to 13; use a 2-decimal preset (Dimension1-6) or raise Precision.
cards.applies_to: dimension objects drawn with CorelDRAW's Dimension tools (Parallel, Horizontal or Vertical, Angular, Segment; Toolbox > Dimension flyout): sets the dimension line's outline and arrowheads, the label's font and colour and the label format (decimal places, units shown, placement, box); not for ordinary lines, text or callouts
cards.how_to_apply: Pick a dimension tool (Parallel Dimension: Toolbox > Dimension flyout, Automation.InvokeItem("f1b16e8a-9f6f-05b4-4610-451172f5fff2")) and choose 'Dimension8' where the tool lists its presets (the harvest records the preset file, not the property-bar control): Custom Data/DimensionPresets.cdss in the CorelDRAW install folder, style Dimension8. Script: no harvested call applies a .cdss dimension preset; reproduce it with Layer.CreateLinearDimension(..., Precision=0, ShowUnits=True, Placement=2, BoxedText=True, LeadingZero=True, OutlineWidth=hairline, Arrows=triangle arrowheads, TextFont="Arial", TextSize=12, ...) or edit an existing dimension through Shape.Dimension (Precision, Placement, BoxedText, ShowUnits, Outline) (untested).

verified.note: No thumbnail (dimension preset, not visual); every stated value checked against DimensionPresets.cdss and matches.

cards.name: circle
cards.summary: Displacement map for Effects > Distort > Displace. The thumbnail is the map file itself (circle.bmp, a tiny 10 x 10 px RGB tile shown enlarged), not a displaced image: soft concentric square rings, magenta-violet at the corners fading to teal at the centre. Measured: red climbs from 81 at the centre to 191 at the corners while green falls from 191 to 81, so the shift depends on distance from each tile's centre; tiled, it should give a repeating grid of round lens or bubble-glass distortions. The colours are only the encoding: blue is flat, red and green carry the shift (assumed Photoshop convention: red horizontal, green vertical, 128 = no shift; not checked in CorelDRAW).
use_for: repeating lens or bubble-glass distortion over a background photo
op-art backgrounds from a plain photo or gradient
avoid: Faces and small type: even the default Horizontal / Vertical 10 can tear detail; keep values low or apply it to the background only.
Large images with Tile: a 10 px tile repeats hundreds of times into a fine, mechanical pattern; use Stretch to fit for one big distortion.
Wanting the pattern to show: the map only moves pixels, its greys and colours never appear; for a visible texture use a bitmap pattern fill.
The look is unverified on a real image: the thumbnail is the map file, not a displaced picture; preview in the dialog first.
Scripts: the harvested map list (CurrentDisplaceImage) was empty, so Bitmap.ApplyBitmapEffect cannot pick this map reliably; apply it from the dialog.
Vector art that must stay vector: the result rasterises at output; use the Envelope or Distort tools for vector warps.
cards.applies_to: bitmaps (imported photos, rasterised art); from the Effects menu CorelDRAW 2024 also takes vector objects as a non-destructive effect. The map is not applied on its own: it is the displacement map chosen inside Effects > Distort > Displace
cards.how_to_apply: Select the bitmap, Effects > Distort > Displace (menu GUID e927013f-df8a-4c2f-89dd-15e351a9d559), pick 'circle' in the dialog's map list, set Tile or Stretch to fit, Horizontal / Vertical (0-100, default 10) and Undefined Areas (Repeat Edges / Wrap Around), OK; the effect stays editable in the Properties docker's effect stack. File: Custom Data/Displace/circle.bmp in the CorelDRAW install folder. Script: shape.Bitmap.ApplyBitmapEffect("Displace", "DisplaceEffect ScaleMode=Tile,HorizontalScale=40,VerticalScale=40,UndefinedArea=0,CurrentDisplaceImage=<map>") is the harvested command template, but the map list read empty in the harvest, so which map a script gets is unknown (untested).

verified.note: 10 x 10 map file: concentric square rings, magenta-violet corners to teal centre; measured R 81 centre to 191 corners, G the reverse, B flat 191, as described.

review.changes: install path in how_to_apply made relative (no machine paths)

cards.summary: Displacement map for Effects > Distort > Displace. The thumbnail is the map file itself (worms.bmp, 100 x 100 px greyscale), not a displaced image: about 60 short squiggly strokes, half white and half black, in random directions on mid-grey. Expected result: small organic wiggles across the image, a wormy, heat-haze or psychedelic wobble. Greyscale map: mid-grey means no shift, lighter and darker values push pixels in opposite directions.
use_for: organic squiggle distortion on a background photo
psychedelic or heat-haze wobble on rasterised type
avoid: Faces and small type: even the default Horizontal / Vertical 10 can tear detail; keep values low or apply it to the background only.
Wanting the pattern to show: the map only moves pixels, its greys and colours never appear; for a visible texture use a bitmap pattern fill.
The look is unverified on a real image: the thumbnail is the map file, not a displaced picture; preview in the dialog first.
Scripts: the harvested map list (CurrentDisplaceImage) was empty, so Bitmap.ApplyBitmapEffect cannot pick this map reliably; apply it from the dialog.
Vector art that must stay vector: the result rasterises at output; use the Envelope or Distort tools for vector warps.
cards.applies_to: bitmaps (imported photos, rasterised art); from the Effects menu CorelDRAW 2024 also takes vector objects as a non-destructive effect. The map is not applied on its own: it is the displacement map chosen inside Effects > Distort > Displace
cards.how_to_apply: Select the bitmap, Effects > Distort > Displace (menu GUID e927013f-df8a-4c2f-89dd-15e351a9d559), pick 'worms' in the dialog's map list, set Tile or Stretch to fit, Horizontal / Vertical (0-100, default 10) and Undefined Areas (Repeat Edges / Wrap Around), OK; the effect stays editable in the Properties docker's effect stack. File: Custom Data/Displace/worms.bmp in the CorelDRAW install folder. Script: shape.Bitmap.ApplyBitmapEffect("Displace", "DisplaceEffect ScaleMode=Tile,HorizontalScale=40,VerticalScale=40,UndefinedArea=0,CurrentDisplaceImage=<map>") is the harvested command template, but the map list read empty in the harvest, so which map a script gets is unknown (untested).

verified.note: 100 x 100 greyscale map: about 60 short squiggly strokes, half white half black, in random directions on mid-grey, as described.

review.changes: install path in how_to_apply made relative (no machine paths)
